name: Topic 31: Hydration in hot and humid climates (Mumbai)
defaultTargetFormula: target_ml = topic30_target_ml + heat_add_ml; heat_add_ml = min(band_add + outdoor_add + commute_add, 1000); band_add: comfortable 0, warm_humid 300, hot_humid 500 (same as Topic 30 hot_weather toggle), very_hot 750; outdoor_add 500 if outdoor sun work 2h or more; commute_add 250 if commute 60 min or more; clamp result 1500-4500 ml; round to nearest 50 ml; ceiling 250 ml per 15-20 min and 1400 ml per hour. All heat adds are FitPlate estimates (est.); ICMR-NIN 2020 hot-climate water values Not found.

drinks.name: Plain water
drinks.notes: First choice in heat; safe boiled or filtered water

drinks.name: Nimbu pani with a pinch of salt
drinks.notes: est.; about 200 mg sodium per glass (calc., est.); 1-2 teaspoons sugar

drinks.name: Chaas (salted buttermilk)
drinks.notes: est.; about 300-500 mg sodium per glass (secondary, unverified); counts toward Topic 18

drinks.name: Tender coconut water
drinks.notes: est.; potassium about 221-361 mg per 100 ml, varies by maturity (secondary, unverified); Topic 19

drinks.name: Torani or aam panna
drinks.notes: est.; traditional heat-wave drinks; sugar and salt vary

drinks.name: ORS (WHO reduced osmolarity)
drinks.notes: For diarrhoea, vomiting or heat illness only; 75 mmol/L sodium, 75 mmol/L glucose; not a daily drink

drinks.name: Sports or electrolyte drink
drinks.notes: est.; sugar and sodium; only for 2 hours or more of sweaty effort

drinks.name: Chai or coffee
drinks.notes: est.; caffeine; Indian heat advisories say limit; Topic 30

drinks.name: Fruit juice or soft drink
drinks.notes: est.; product policy because of sugar

drinksTable.notes: First choice; cool, not ice-cold, is easier to drink in quantity (est.)
Sodium about 200 mg per glass (est., calc.); keep sugar to 1-2 teaspoons (est.)
About 300-500 mg sodium per glass (secondary, unverified); potassium, protein
Potassium about 221-361 mg/100 ml; sodium low to moderate; values vary (secondary, unverified); Topic 19
Traditional heat-wave drinks in MoHFW/NDMA lists; sugar and salt vary
75 mmol/L sodium, 75 mmol/L glucose; for illness or heat illness only, as per sachet
Sugar and sodium; for 2 hours or more of sweaty effort
Caffeine; Indian heat advisories say limit tea and coffee; fine in moderation (Topic 30)
Worsens heat illness; avoid in heat (NDMA list)

reminderRules.rule: Keep the Topic 30 schedule (09:30, 11:30, 13:30, 15:30, 17:30, 19:30, about 250 ml each); on hot-humid or very hot days add 08:30 (before commute) and 16:30 (before evening commute); maximum 8 per day (est.)
reminderRules.source: FitPlate design (est.); NDMA/MoHFW advice to drink often even if not thirsty (secondary)

reminderRules.rule: Outdoor workers: prompt every 60-90 minutes during work hours; suggested sip no more than 250 ml per 15-20 minutes and no more than 1,400 ml per hour
reminderRules.source: OSHA/NIOSH heat infosheet (1 cup every 15-20 min, 48 oz per hour limit; secondary); FitPlate design (est.)

reminderRules.rule: No reminders 21:00-07:00; skip if a drink was logged in the last 60 minutes; stop when target met
Show ORS prompt only after logged vomiting, loose motions or faintness in heat; never as a daily preset
Heat red-flag report (confusion, fit, hot dry skin, no sweating, fainting): show 'Call 108/102 now', stop prompts
reminderRules.source: NHS heat exhaustion and heatstroke guidance; MoHFW/NPCCHH heat-illness manuals (secondary)

reminderRules.rule: Doctor-flag users (kidney, heart, liver, fluid limit, diuretics), pregnancy with swelling or high BP, and children: no extra-fluid or salt prompts; show 'Follow your doctor's advice'
reminderRules.source: FitPlate safety design; kidney charity and dialysis guidance (patient pages, not guidelines); CDC pregnancy and heat

warnings: Heat stroke signs (confusion, fits, hot dry skin, collapse) are an emergency: call 108 or 102.
Do not drink more than about 1,400 ml per hour; over-drinking can cause low blood sodium.
No salt tablets; use food and chaas or nimbu pani; people with BP, kidney or heart disease should not add salt without advice.
ORS is for illness, not for daily use.
Children, older adults, pregnant or breastfeeding women, and people with kidney, heart or liver disease need a doctor's guidance; the app shows no extra-fluid rules for them.
ICMR-NIN 2020 hot-climate water values and official IMD monthly tables were not accessed; climate figures are secondary and heat adds are FitPlate estimates.
